text.content:
Some West African shamans draw their power from their ancestors instead of the Spirits of Man. An ancestor shaman still follows an animal totem and otherwise uses the normal magic rules.

  • They summon ancestor spirits instead of any other Spirits of Man, and conjure other nature spirits normally. Totem bonuses for conjuring Spirits of Man apply to ancestor spirits.
  • Ancestor-spirit shamanic adepts conjure only ancestor spirits and cast only spells their totem favors. Ancestral conjuring adepts summon whatever an ancestor shaman can, but have no Sorcery.
  • Any shaman may conjure ancestor spirits, whatever the totem: swap one of the totem's conjuring bonuses for a bonus to ancestor spirits (gamemaster and player agree which).
  • Fetishes: summoning takes three fetishes tied to that ancestor — usually one object made for them before death (a stool, say) and two things they enjoyed in life. Each one missing costs the spirit 1 service.
  • Time: hours equal to the spirit's Force, divided by the number of the spirit's relatives present (the shaman included; they needn't be willing). Services and Drain are normal.
  • No Great Form or Ally ancestor spirits are known.
  • They come from a "plane of death" shaped by the summoner's own beliefs. A shaman can quest there for their totem only with an ancestor spirit as guide (metaplane rules: Grimoire p.93).

Play them like living relatives. Cyberpirates p.152.

BQSCIWERAttacks
F + 2F × 3F + 1FFFF(A)F(Strength)M Stun

Powers: Accident, Confusion, Divination, Guard, Manifestation, Search.

"× 3" is the running multiplier when manifested. Ancestor spirits have no domain: their powers reach 5 km per point of Force.

Not yet summonable in Foundry: its (Strength)M Stun attack needs a system change (the system's spirit attacks take their Power from Force). Until then, run it from this page. Cyberpirates p.152.

Asked to prophesy, the spirit reads the emotions and drives of everyone within its powers' area and guesses what they will do next. The gamemaster rolls dice equal to the spirit's Force against a TN set by the question:

The question isTN
Very vague ("What does next month hold for me?")4
Vague ("Are my old enemies catching up?")5
General ("Will I get hurt on this job?")6
Specific ("Is this official taking bribes?")8
Very specific ("What is the name of the man following me?")10
  • 0 successes: a cryptic answer, often badly misleading.
  • 1–2: cryptic, but with a truth underneath.
  • 3–4: mildly helpful.
  • 5+: about the detail the questioner wanted.

The answer is at most twice the spirit's Force in words, and as specific or vague as suits the story. Cyberpirates p.152.
